name: Omni Content – AI Blog Writer, Content Calendar & Approval Workflow
author: kevaliai

sections.description:
Omni Content combines an AI blog writer with a content calendar and editorial approval workflow for WordPress. Create drafts, improve selected text, collaborate with reviewers, and schedule approved posts from one plugin.

Designed for bloggers, small businesses, content teams, freelancers, and agencies managing editorial work, Omni Content keeps people in control of what gets published. AI generation is delivered through the Omni Content service; you do not need to configure your own OpenAI or Anthropic API key to use that service.

AI Writing and Editing

  • Generate structured blog post drafts with AI.
  • Set language, tone, keywords, and custom instructions.
  • Improve, rephrase, expand, shorten, or correct grammar in selected draft text.
  • Accept or reject suggested changes before saving.

Content Calendar and Publishing

  • Organize planned content in a calendar.
  • Save draft briefs and planned dates without automatically starting generation.
  • Schedule approved posts for publication.
  • Keep editorial review in the publishing process.

Team Review and Accountability

  • Configure roles and permissions for content workflows.
  • Review and approve drafts before publication.
  • Track review, approval, and publishing activity in an audit trail.
  • Configure workflow notification templates and role-based emails.

Subscriptions and Usage

  • Start with an available Free plan; optional Pro and Agency plans are offered through Freemius.
  • View remaining word and image allowances and the next usage reset date.
  • Review available plans, billing cycles, and supported license quantities in the Subscription screen.
  • Open subscription management, cancellation, and refund-request options through Freemius.

Plan allowances, license quantities, prices, and feature availability are shown in the plugin’s Subscription screen and may change. Each license activates Omni Content on one WordPress site; Agency plans include additional site licenses for teams managing several sites.

Email and Support

  • Configure SMTP or Mailchimp Transactional (Mandrill) for workflow notifications.
  • Send administrator-only test emails.
  • Customize workflow email templates.
  • Submit support requests from inside the plugin.

Before You Publish

AI-generated content may contain factual errors, unsuitable material, or incorrect links. Review facts, formatting, sources, copyright considerations, and other important details before publication.

External Services

Omni Content connects to external services when the corresponding feature is configured or used. These services may process information outside your WordPress installation. Review their terms and privacy policies before using each service.

Omni Content / Keval AI API

The plugin connects to the Omni Content / Keval AI API for account connection, subscriptions, usage information, public templates, content generation, and content-improvement features. AI generation through this service does not require a separately supplied OpenAI or Anthropic API key.

Data sent may include the site domain and URL, site name, WordPress version, PHP version, plugin version, license information, account name and email, selected plan, template identifiers and fields, prompts, blog brief, keywords, custom instructions, generated content, image brief, report filters, and generation identifiers.

Data is sent when an administrator connects or activates an Omni Content account or subscription, loads remote templates or account information, requests content generation or improvement, or views remote usage reports. The plugin must not transmit this information before the administrator explicitly starts the connection or related service action.

Service provider: Keval AI / Omni Content

  • Terms of Service: https://keval.ai/terms
  • Privacy Policy: https://keval.ai/privacy-policy

Freemius

The plugin uses the bundled Freemius SDK for account connection, license activation, subscription status, pricing, and hosted checkout for optional paid plans. Paid purchases and subscription management use Freemius account and checkout flows.

Data processed may include the account name and email, site URL, installation identifier, WordPress, PHP and plugin versions, license and plan identifiers, selected billing cycle, license quantity, and checkout or billing details entered in the hosted checkout.

Data is exchanged when an administrator connects the installation, activates or synchronizes a license, views subscription pricing, starts checkout, or opens account, cancellation, or refund-request options. Optional SDK data collection is subject to the connection choices shown by Freemius.

Service provider: Freemius

  • Terms of Service: https://freemius.com/terms/
  • Privacy Policy: https://freemius.com/privacy/

Facebook Graph API

The plugin can use the Facebook Graph API to publish selected content to a configured Facebook Page.

Data sent includes the sharing message, Facebook Page identifier, and configured Page access token. Data is sent only when Facebook sharing is configured and an authorized user requests sharing.

Service provider: Meta / Facebook

  • Meta Platform Terms: https://developers.facebook.com/terms
  • Meta Privacy Policy: https://www.facebook.com/privacy/policy/

X Share Intent

The plugin can open an X share-intent page containing prefilled text. This opens a user-facing browser page and does not automatically publish through the X API.

Data sent includes the sharing text placed in the share URL. It is sent only when a user selects the X sharing option.

Service provider: X Corp.

  • Terms of Service: https://x.com/en/tos
  • Privacy Policy: https://x.com/en/privacy

Google Fonts and Favicon Service

The plugin may request Google Fonts on designated administration screens and favicon images when displaying sources. These requests may disclose standard connection information, including an IP address, user agent, referrer, requested font family, or requested favicon domain.

Requests are made when a relevant administration screen is viewed or a source favicon is displayed. Site administrators should review this behavior before enabling related functionality.

Service provider: Google

  • Google Fonts Terms: https://developers.google.com/fonts/terms
  • Google Privacy Policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

Remote Image Hosts

When generated content contains a remote image URL, the plugin can request that image and import it into the WordPress media library. The image host may receive the server IP address and requested URL.

The request is made when an authorized user saves or schedules generated content containing a remote image and chooses to use the image. The provider depends on the returned image URL; users should review that provider’s terms and privacy policy.

Optional License-Verification Endpoint

An administrator may configure a custom endpoint for license verification. This is a license-verification setting, not an option to configure a third-party AI generation provider. The endpoint may receive the license key, license email, site URL, admin URL, and product identifier.

Data is sent only when an administrator configures the endpoint and requests verification. The administrator is responsible for reviewing the endpoint provider’s terms and privacy policy.

Configured Email Provider and Support Requests

When email delivery is configured, the plugin sends test messages, workflow notifications, and submitted support requests through the administrator’s SMTP server or Mailchimp Transactional (Mandrill).

The provider receives the configured sender details, recipient email addresses, subject, message body, and credentials needed to authenticate the request. Workflow messages may contain post titles, author names, event dates, and other content included in the saved email template. Support requests send the site URL, subject, and message to the Omni Content support team when an authorized user submits the support form.

Messages are sent when an administrator requests a delivery test, a configured workflow event occurs, or an authorized user submits a support request. Failed workflow deliveries may be retried. Administrators using SMTP should review their selected provider’s terms and privacy policy.

When Mailchimp Transactional is configured:

  • Mailchimp Standard Terms of Use: https://mailchimp.com/legal/terms/
  • Mailchimp Privacy Policy: https://mailchimp.com/legal/privacy/
sections.installation:
1. Install Omni Content from the WordPress plugin directory, or upload the omni-content folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate the plugin from the Plugins screen.
  3. Open Omni Content in the WordPress administration menu.
  4. Review the external-service disclosures and connect or configure only the services you want to use.
  5. Review the available plan and usage allowances in Omni Content > Subscription.
  6. Configure your content and approval preferences, then create your first draft.
sections.faq:
Do I need an OpenAI or Anthropic API key?

No separate OpenAI or Anthropic API key is required for generation through the Omni Content service. Connect the plugin to the Omni Content service and use the allowances available on your plan.

Can I use Omni Content with a team?

Yes. Omni Content includes roles, permissions, review controls, approval tracking, and workflow email notifications.

Does Omni Content publish without approval?

Publishing behavior depends on the workflow configured by the administrator. Review and approval can be required before publication, while authorized administrators may enable automatic publishing for approved content.

Is Omni Content suitable for agencies with multiple sites?

Yes. The Agency plan includes additional site licenses through Freemius, so you can run Omni Content on each client site. Each site keeps its own workflow, roles, and approvals. Check Omni Content > Subscription for current license allowances.

What is included in the Free plan?

An available Free plan lets you get started with 5,000 words of AI content generation and 5 AI image generations. Current word and image allowances, reset dates, and any plan-specific restrictions are displayed in Omni Content > Subscription. Upgrade to Pro or Agency for additional usage limits and advanced functionality.

Should I review AI-generated content?

Yes. AI-generated material may be inaccurate, incomplete, or unsuitable. Review facts, links, formatting, copyright considerations, and other important details before publication.

How do I manage or cancel my subscription?

Open Omni Content > Subscription to view your connected plan, usage allowances, and available upgrade options. Paid checkout and account management use Freemius. Cancellation and refund-request options open the corresponding Freemius flow; submitting a refund request does not automatically issue a refund.

How do I configure email notifications?

Open Omni Content settings and select the Email tab. Save your SMTP or Mailchimp Transactional credentials, then send a test email. Configure email templates and workflow role assignments for the notifications you want to send.
sections.changelog:
1.1.0

  • Changed: Migrated the subscription screen and paid checkout flow to the bundled Freemius SDK.
  • Added: Free, Pro, and Agency plan options, billing-cycle selection, and supported license quantities.
  • Added: Remaining word and image usage meters, the usage reset date, and account, cancellation, and refund-request links.
  • Added: Selected-content AI tools for improvement, rephrasing, grammar correction, expansion, and shortening, with accept and reject controls.
  • Added: SMTP and Mailchimp Transactional settings, encrypted credential storage, and administrator-only test emails.
  • Added: Customizable workflow email templates, role-based notifications, and an in-plugin support request form.
  • Fixed: Account activation and legacy subscription links now route to registered WordPress administration pages.
  • Fixed: Connected Free-plan wallets are retained in the generator instead of being replaced by a legacy response that incorrectly shows Activate Plan.
  • Fixed: Saving a calendar draft preserves its brief, date, and time without scheduling content generation.
  • Fixed: Workflow emails avoid duplicate notifications, retry failed recipients, and wait for actual publication before sending publication notices.
  • Improved: Subscription state is synchronized from the Freemius SDK rather than trusting checkout return parameters.
  • Improved: Subscription pricing uses Freemius catalog data and shows unavailable states when pricing or usage cannot be retrieved.
  • Improved: Checkout and email-setting actions validate administrator permissions and request nonces.

1.0.0

  • First public WordPress.org release.
  • Added AI-assisted blog post generation.
  • Added content planning and scheduling tools.
  • Added review, approval, role, and permission controls.
  • Added publishing and workflow activity tracking.

screenshots.caption: Content Generator — Search and filter templates by category, switch between grid and list views, and select Use Template to start a draft.
Generated Blog Editor — Edit the generated title and body in Visual or Code mode, check the word count, then copy the draft or send it for review.
Plans — Compare Free, Pro, and Agency features and allowances, check your remaining words and images and the renewal date, and manage billing.
Marketing Calendar — Browse the monthly queue of drafts, scheduled posts, and published posts. Select a date to start a brief or open an existing post to revisit its saved details.
Calendar Brief — Set the date and template, enter the topic, tone, keywords, and other brief details, then select Save as Draft or Content Generate.
Review Board — View workflow status totals, filter the queue by status, blog type, author, or date range, and select Open to review a draft.
Omni Content Reports — Filter generated content by date, template, or title, track word and image usage over time, and export the results as a CSV file.
